sections.h2: Contacting the Monroe County recording office
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds is in Room 106 of the Administration Building at One Quaker Plaza in Stroudsburg. The main number is 570-517-3969, and the fax line is 570-517-3873. Doors open at 8:30 in the morning and close at 4:30 in the afternoon on weekdays, with major holidays off.

Walk-in recording and title searches are available, though appointments are strongly encouraged because space is limited. Packages can also arrive by post, or electronically through Simplifile, CSC and EPN. Record books begin in 1836, the year Monroe County was formed from parts of Northampton and Pike counties, and filings made since August 1995 sit on the Landex system.

Along with the recording fee, the office collects realty transfer tax for the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue and for every municipality and school district in the county. It also collects for the Monroe County Affordable Housing Agency, the Commonwealth Court Computer Automation fund, the Equal Access to Justice program and an archive fund for historical preservation of the land records.

The Recorder also runs a free Record Alert System, which sends a notice whenever a document is filed under the subscriber's name. An owner who wants to know about any filing against a property can sign up.

A deed or mortgage costs $87.75 under the fee bill that took effect November 17, 2025 and was revised the next day with no fee increase. The bill adds $2.00 for each page over four, $0.50 for each name over four, and $10.00 for each tax code number on a document.

Transfer tax is 1 percent state and 1 percent local. The fee bill also sets payment rules. Personal checks are turned away, the exact amount is required because the office makes no change and gives no refunds, and a rejected document adds a $2.00 charge. Include a postage-paid return envelope so originals can come back.

sections.h2: What a Monroe County deed must contain
sections.html:
The office wants an original that is signed, dated and acknowledged in front of a notary, showing the notary's seal, signature and expiration date. Fees and transfer taxes are due the moment the deed is presented.

  • A tax code number for the parcel.
  • A property description that names the municipality.
  • Payment of the transfer tax. If the tax is unpaid or the deed does not show true value, as with a $1.00 deed, a Statement of Value goes in as two copies and the office forwards it to the state.
  • A return envelope with postage already on it.

Staff will not draft a deed for anyone. Once recorded, a deed stays as written, so adding a spouse or fixing an error means recording a new deed or a deed of correction. Originals go back to the buyer, and mortgages go to the lender. On the lender side, Act 197 lets a satisfaction piece be recorded without the original mortgage or a certified copy of it.

sections.h2: Who pays transfer tax on a sale?
sections.html:
The state share and the municipal share are 1 percent apiece, applied to the property's value, which can differ from the sale price. Contracts often split the bill between seller and buyer. Even so, a deed is turned away unless the tax is paid when it is presented, and the new owner carries the risk if the amount is questioned later.

Family exemptions cover a husband and wife, parent to child, grandparent to grandchild, and brothers and sisters, plus deeds between former spouses. Non-profit corporations get no break. Deeds handed to government units and property that passes by inheritance are also exempt.

A state investigator can decide that a property was worth more than the value stated, or that a claimed exemption fails. The Department of Revenue then mails the owner a determination. Extra tax and interest are paid to the state, a matching municipal sum is paid at the recorder's office, and the deed is recorded again for regular fees.

sections.h2: Unpaid property tax and the Tax Claim Bureau
sections.html:
Delinquent real estate taxes go to the Monroe County Tax Claim Bureau, which handles 20 municipalities and four school districts and receives about 9,000 delinquent returns a year. It exists under Act 542 of 1947, the Pennsylvania Real Estate Tax Sale Law, with the aim of putting tax-delinquent properties back on the productive rolls.

The bureau is down the hall in Room 104 of the same building, at 570-517-3172, and works weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30. A seller with overdue taxes should request a lien certificate so the closing agent can see what must come out of the proceeds. Counter payments can be made with a money order, a cashier's check or a card, and repository sales run through Bid4Assets.

If you are behind on taxes, call the bureau before listing, because the balance has to be settled as part of any sale.

sections.h2: Steps for a Monroe County sale
sections.html:
Start with the tax side. Request the lien certificate if anything is owed. Next, confirm the municipality and the parcel's tax code number, since both go on the deed. At closing the deed is signed and acknowledged before a notary. Your closing agent then files it with the transfer tax and recording fee, either electronically or at Room 106, and the original goes back to the buyer. Because personal checks are refused and no change is given, the payment form and exact amount are worth confirming the day before.

If a family member is receiving the house, tell the closing agent so the exemption is claimed correctly on the deed or a Statement of Value.

Stroudsburg is the county seat of this Pocono county in northeast Pennsylvania, which had 168,327 people in 2020. The 2020 census listed 79,114 housing units, 21.3 percent of them vacant, and about three in four occupied homes (76.6 percent) had an owner living in them. Vacation and second-home use is part of the market here, so expect buyers from outside the county and have your tax code number and municipality ready when they ask. Public schools run through four districts: East Stroudsburg Area, Pleasant Valley, Pocono Mountain and Stroudsburg Area.

faqs.q: What is the Monroe County deed recording fee?
faqs.a: A deed or mortgage starts at $87.75. The bill adds $2.00 for every page past four, $0.50 for every name past four, and $10.00 for each tax code number on the document.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Monroe County recording fee with a personal check?
faqs.a: No. Personal checks are not accepted, and the exact amount is required, with no change or refunds. Ask the office which payment forms it takes before sending a package.
Yes. Simplifile, CSC and EPN are the three e-recording routes, and paper still works by post or at the Stroudsburg counter.

faqs.q: Which Monroe County deeds are exempt from transfer tax?
faqs.a: Family deeds between spouses, down the line from parent or grandparent, or among brothers and sisters are exempt, and so are deeds between ex-spouses. Non-profit corporations are not exempt. For any other case, talk to an attorney.

faqs.q: Who collects overdue Monroe County property tax?
faqs.a: The Tax Claim Bureau, Room 104 at One Quaker Plaza in Stroudsburg. Its counter takes money orders, cashier's checks and cards, and the bureau can issue a lien certificate for a sale.
